conversation.content: I want to start selling my handmade mugs on one of the big handmade marketplaces. No hard deadline, but I'd love a first sale within three months. I have ~8 hours a week and about $500 to start. Kiln access twice a week at my community studio.

current_state.summary: Has made about 40 mugs in the last year, gifted most of them; never sold anything.

resources: Community studio membership with kiln access twice a week
goal.title: Open an online shop selling my ceramic mugs

alternatives_considered.option: Launch immediately with the mugs you already have
alternatives_considered.why_not: Without costs and fees you risk pricing below cost.

decision_summary.impact: About 8 hours a week; the $500 budget goes to materials, packaging and possible listing fees.
decision_summary.what_changed: Created a 3-region route aimed at a first sale in about 13 weeks.
decision_summary.why: Costs and capacity come first because they decide the price and the size of the first collection.

external_claims.claim: Handmade marketplaces charge listing and transaction fees.

external_claims.affects: Price per mug and what can be listed (task n1)
external_claims.claim: Exact current fee levels and rules for food-contact ceramics on the chosen marketplace.

assumptions.statement: A first sale within about 3 months is the target, not a hard deadline.

goal.desired_outcome: A live marketplace shop with at least 10 listed mugs and a first sale.
resources: Community studio membership with kiln access twice a week
success_criteria: Shop live with at least 10 listings
goal.title: Open an online shop selling my ceramic mugs

success_criteria: Cost sheet with materials, firing, packaging and marketplace fees
milestones.title: Price per mug decided from real costs

success_criteria: Shop profile and policies filled in
milestones.title: Shop ready to publish

success_criteria: First order from a stranger shipped
milestones.title: First sale

task.description: On each marketplace's official seller pages, find listing fees, transaction and payment-processing fees, and any rules for handmade items and food-contact ceramics. Record each with the page link and today's date.
task.expected_result: A short table per marketplace with fees, relevant rules and source links.
task.title: Write down the current fees and seller rules of 2 candidate marketplaces

acceptance_criteria: Every fee has a source link
methods.instructions: Submit the table with one row per fee or rule and a link to the official page for each.
The navigator opens the linked pages to confirm they are official seller documentation.

pass_criteria: Fees and rules recorded with official source links
verification_protocol.rationale: Research results are checkable against their sources.

task.why_it_matters: Fees go straight into your price, and food-contact rules may affect what you can list. These change over time, so they must come from the official source.

nodes.title: Check current marketplace fees and seller rules

task.description: Using receipts and studio fees, calculate clay, glaze, firing share, packaging and shipping materials per mug. Add a row for your time at an hourly rate you choose.
task.expected_result: A spreadsheet with cost per mug broken down into at least 5 lines.
task.title: Build a cost sheet for one mug from your last 10 pieces

methods.instructions: A question on the biggest cost driver.
questions: Which cost line surprised you most?

pass_criteria: Complete cost sheet with a per-mug total

task.why_it_matters: Without real costs you can't set a price that pays for materials, fees and some of your time.

task.description: For the next two weeks, log each studio session — mugs thrown, trimmed, glazed, fired, and losses.
task.expected_result: A 2-week production log and an estimate of finished mugs per month.
task.title: Log 2 weeks of production and estimate mugs per month

methods.instructions: Fill in the log per session.

pass_criteria: Monthly estimate derived from the log
verification_protocol.rationale: A session-level log is structured and internally checkable, though entered by the user.

task.why_it_matters: Capacity decides how big the first collection can be and whether restocking is realistic.

nodes.title: Measure monthly capacity with two kiln slots

options: Launch discount for the first 5 buyers
decision.question: Which pricing approach for launch?

nodes.title: Make and select a first collection of 10 mugs
Photograph the collection in natural light (3 photos per mug)
Publish the shop and share it with 30 people you know
30-day review of views, favourites and sales

journey.strategy_summary: Validate unit economics and capacity first, then build a small, well-photographed first collection, launch, and learn from the first 30 days of traffic.

expected_output.message_to_user:
Here's your route to a first sale in about three months. It starts with the unglamorous part that decides whether the shop can work at all: what one mug really costs you, and how many you can make per month with two kiln slots a week.
Marketplace fees and seller rules change, so the first region includes checking them on the marketplace's official pages before you set prices — I haven't assumed any numbers.
Later regions (listing photos, launch, first sales) are outlines for now and will get detailed once we know your costs and capacity.

contrastive.critique: Presents specific fee numbers as verified with a source that was never researched, and the route is generic (research, market, sell) without costs or capacity.

external_claims.claim: Listing fee is $0.20 and the transaction fee is 6.5%.

goal.title: Open an online shop selling my ceramic mugs

output.message_to_user: Great! The marketplace charges a $0.20 listing fee and 6.5% per sale, so price your mugs at $25 and start selling.
